claim: Site-to-Site VPN supports Diffie-Hellman groups 2 and 14-24 in Phase 1, and groups 2, 5 and 14-24 in Phase 2.
q: Which Diffie-Hellman groups does Site-to-Site VPN support?

claim: Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators currently support 5 Gbps aggregate bandwidth, and each site can support a maximum of 100 Mbps.
q: What bandwidth does a Site-to-Site VPN Concentrator support in total and per site?
v: Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators support 5 Gbps aggregate bandwidth
Each site can support a maximum of 100 Mbps bandwidth
scope: per Site-to-Site VPN Concentrator and per site
cond: AWS Support can be asked for higher bandwidth
ev: Currently, Site-to-Site VPN Concentrators support 5 Gbps aggregate bandwidth. Each site can support a maximum of 100 Mbps bandwidth. However, if you need higher bandwidth, reach out to AWS Support.

claim: A transit gateway shows only the preferred route: the routes received from the Direct Connect gateway are preferred, and the Site-to-Site VPN is the backup route that shows only when the Direct Connect gateway route is no longer advertised.
q: On a transit gateway, which path is preferred for the same prefix learned over Direct Connect and over Site-to-Site VPN?
v: the routes received from the Direct Connect gateway route, which is the preferred route
The Site-to-Site VPN, which is the backup route, will only display when the Direct Connect gateway is no longer advertised
ev: AWS Transit Gateway will only show the routes received from the Direct Connect gateway route, which is the preferred route. The Site-to-Site VPN, which is the backup route, will only display when the Direct Connect gateway is no longer advertised.

claim: ECMP is not supported between different attachment types on a transit gateway; for example you cannot enable ECMP between a VPN and a VPC attachment. Routes are evaluated and traffic goes to the evaluated route instead.
q: Can a transit gateway use ECMP across a VPN attachment and another attachment type?
v: ECMP is not supported between different attachment types
you can't enable ECMP between a VPN and a VPC attachment
ev: ECMP is not supported between different attachment types. For example, you can't enable ECMP between a VPN and a VPC attachment. Instead, transit gateway routes are evaluated and traffic routed accordingly to the evaluated route.

claim: You can connect a Site-to-Site VPN attachment to a transit gateway to connect your VPCs and on-premises networks. Both dynamic and static routes are supported, as well as IPv4 and IPv6.
q: What routing and IP versions does a Site-to-Site VPN attachment on a transit gateway support?
v: connect a Site-to-Site VPN attachment to a transit gateway
Both dynamic and static routes are supported, as well as IPv4 and IPv6
ev: You can connect a Site-to-Site VPN attachment to a transit gateway in AWS Transit Gateway, allowing you to connect your VPCs and on-premises networks. Both dynamic and static routes are supported, as well as IPv4 and IPv6.

claim: A single Direct Connect gateway supports ECMP across multiple transit virtual interfaces, so AWS recommends using only a single Direct Connect gateway rather than several gateways to get ECMP.
q: Does a Direct Connect gateway support ECMP across transit virtual interfaces?
v: A single Direct Connect gateway supports ECMP across multiple transit virtual interfaces
we recommended that you set up and use only a single Direct Connect gateway
scope: Direct Connect gateway with transit virtual interfaces
ev: A single Direct Connect gateway supports ECMP across multiple transit virtual interfaces. Therefore, we recommended that you set up and use only a single Direct Connect gateway and to not set up and use multiple gateways to take advantage of ECMP.

claim: A Direct Connect gateway is a globally available service that distributes routing information like a BGP route reflector. Data does not pass through it; it only handles routing information.
q: Does data traffic pass through a Direct Connect gateway?
v: Data does not pass through a DXGW – it only handles the routing information
behaving similarly to BGP route reflectors in a traditional network
ev: Direct Connect Gateway (DXGW) is a globally available service that distributes routing information across its connections, behaving similarly to BGP route reflectors in a traditional network. Data does not pass through a DXGW – it only handles the routing information.

claim: A virtual private gateway (VGW) is a regional, highly redundant service that provides IP routing and forwarding at the VPC level. It can terminate Site-to-Site VPN connections and Direct Connect private virtual interfaces.
q: What can a virtual private gateway terminate?
v: a regional, highly redundant service that provides IP routing and forwarding at the VPC level
VGW can terminate AWS S2S VPN connections and AWS Direct Connect Private VIFs
ev: AWS Virtual Private Gateway (VGW) is a regional, highly redundant service that provides IP routing and forwarding at the VPC level, acting as the gateway for the VPC to communicate with your customer gateway devices. VGW can terminate AWS S2S VPN connections and AWS Direct Connect Private VIFs.

claim: The accelerated Site-to-Site VPN with transit gateway reference design provides optimized VPN connections over the public internet, and can reach higher bandwidth by configuring multiple VPN tunnels with ECMP.
q: What does the accelerated Site-to-Site VPN with Transit Gateway reference design provide?
v: establish optimized VPN connections over the public internet by using AWS Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections
achieve higher VPN connection bandwidth by configuring multiple VPN tunnels with ECMP
scope: accelerated Site-to-Site VPN with Transit Gateway, single Region
ev: Provide the ability to establish optimized VPN connections over the public internet by using AWS Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections.
Provide the ability to achieve higher VPN connection bandwidth by configuring multiple VPN tunnels with ECMP.

claim: In the whitepaper's worked example, Example Corp. Automotive uses Site-to-Site VPN over the internet to a transit gateway for development and testing, and Direct Connect with a Direct Connect gateway and a second transit gateway for production traffic.
q: How does the hybrid connectivity whitepaper's Example Corp. Automotive example split dev/test and production connectivity?
v: uses AWS S2S VPN over the internet terminating on AWS Transit Gateway for development and testing
uses AWS Direct Connect with Direct Connect gateway and a second AWS Transit Gateway for the production traffic
scope: worked example in the hybrid connectivity whitepaper
ev: It uses AWS S2S VPN over the internet terminating on AWS Transit Gateway for development and testing. It then uses AWS Direct Connect with Direct Connect gateway and a second AWS Transit Gateway for the production traffic.

claim: In the Direct Connect gateway with virtual private gateways design, up to 20 VPCs can be connected per Direct Connect gateway over a single BGP session. If you need more than 20, add Direct Connect gateways or consider Transit Gateway integration.
q: How many VPCs can connect per Direct Connect gateway with virtual private gateways?
v: Up to 20 VPCs can be connected per DXGW over a single BGP session
additional DXGWs can be added to facilitate the connectivity at scale, or consider using Transit Gateway integration
scope: per Direct Connect gateway with virtual private gateways
ev: Up to 20 VPCs can be connected per DXGW over a single BGP session. If more than 20 VPCs are needed, additional DXGWs can be added to facilitate the connectivity at scale, or consider using Transit Gateway integration.
